tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Smooth Local Inverse on an Open Set]

↗ lem:invertible-operators-open

Let $E$ be a Banach space, $F$ a normed space, and $g : E \to F$ a map that is $C^k$ ($k \geq 1$) on an open set $s$ on which $dg_x$ is invertible at every $x \in s$. Let $R$ be the local homeomorphism supplied by the inverse function theorem for $g$, and restrict its domain to $s$. Then $R^{-1}$ is $C^k$ on the whole of the resulting open image $R(s)$.

Proof

↗ lem:invertible-operators-open The set $R(s)$ is open. Let $y \in R(s)$ and put $x = R^{-1}(y) \in s$. Then $g$ is $C^k$ at $x$ and $dg_x$ is invertible, so the inverse function theorem applies at $x$ and shows that $R^{-1}$ is $C^k$ at $g(x) = y$. As $y$ was an arbitrary point of the open set $R(s)$, and a map that is $C^k$ at each point of an open set is $C^k$ on that set, $R^{-1}$ is $C^k$ on $R(s)$. Note that the hypothesis that $dg$ is invertible on all of $s$, rather than at one point only, is what makes this argument available at every $y$; by Lemma 5 it can always be arranged by shrinking $s$.

□
